text:
erin: Quick question — trying to finalize rollout plan for feature_x. If a flag is set at org, project, route, and model levels, which one actually wins at serve time? Example below, want to know what the canary will see.

mike: generally the most-specific scope wins (model overrides route overrides project overrides org). that's been the default since the scope-refactor.

jamie: to add nuance — we recently introduced a route-level "traffic-split" override that can take precedence for requests matched by a route rule. so if the route explicitly marks a flag for canary audiences, it can short-circuit model-level default unless the flag is model-bound.

olivia: hmm can you paste a concrete example? i'm trying to match this to our canary audience planning.

erin: sure — sample config:```yaml
flags:
  org:
    feature_x: false
  project:
    feature_x: true
  route:
    match: "/checkout"
    flags:
      feature_x: false
      feature_x_canary: true
  model:
    feature_x: true
```If a request hits /checkout for a user in canary audience, what should the runtime resolve for feature_x and feature_x_canary?

mike: feature_x -> route is explicit false, model true, so most-specific would be model wins -> true. But because route has feature_x_canary true, the route-level canary marker should apply to routing decision; runtime applies canary markers first to choose variant, then resolves flag values for that variant. So outcome: feature_x_canary=true, then effective feature_x depends on variant-level overrides (in many cases route can force false).

jamie: practically we've seen confusion here. The rule we should document: 1) Determine request routing (audience, route matching). 2) Select variant (canary vs default) if route defines traffic-split. 3) Resolve flag values within selected variant using scope precedence model > route > project > org, except when a flag is explicitly marked as "route-enforced" (these always follow route-level).

olivia: ok so in Erin's YAML: since route has a canary flag, user in canary -> variant=canary. Then within canary, model still wins unless we have route-enforced. So final: feature_x = true (model) and feature_x_canary = true. Is that right?

mike: yes, that's the current behavior. but two caveats: (a) older customers might still be on pre-refactor behavior where route wins; (b) some flags are "guardrail" type and treated as route-enforced to prevent model authors from bypassing safety.

erin: good to know. For rollouts we want route to be able to opt users into canary and guardrails to prevent model teams from flipping critical safety flags. How do we mark a flag as route-enforced?

jamie: flags have metadata field `enforcement_scope: [org|project|route|model]`. When set to `route` it throws away model overrides for that flag. Example in API: `PATCH /flags/feature_x {"enforcement_scope":"route"}`. Only infra-admins can change enforcement_scope.

olivia: where is that documented? i couldn't find it in the flags doc.

mike: not published yet — it landed behind a feature flag in the console. there is an internal RFC: https://go/repo/rfc/flag-enforcement (internal). We should add a short doc in docs/flags and call out the two-step resolution.

erin: action items: 1) Jamie — can you add a one-pager for the team documenting the 3-step resolution (route -> variant selection -> scope precedence) and list the enforcement_scope options? 2) Mike — can you add a console warning when someone tries to set model-level flag that conflicts with a route-enforced flag? 3) Olivia — please add an entry to the rollout checklist about checking enforcement_scope for safety flags.

jamie: yep i'll draft the one-pager and link to RFC. target EOD tomorrow.

mike: I'll open a small console PR for the warning, 2-day cadence.

olivia: I'll update the checklist and ping legal if we need to tag any regulatory-critical flags.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for console-service (PR #4823) — ETA 5m :rocket:

erin: thanks all. last Q — is there telemetry to trace final-resolved-scope so SREs can debug unexpected behavior?

mike: yes — we added `flag_resolution.trace` logs that emit final_resolution={value, source_scope, variant_id} when you enable verbose flag tracing for a tenant. it's off by default.

erin: perfect. that'll make postmortems easier. closing this thread after Jamie's one-pager. :thumbsup:
